newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Airtours summer bookings brighter.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Airtours summer bookings brighter.

text.p: British holiday company Airtours Plc said on Wednesday its UK bookings had risen for the summer, but noted that the rate of increase would probably level out over the year due to capacity constraints.

The company, reporting a sharp reduction in first-quarter losses, said summer bookings in the UK rose 45 percent, while like-for-like bookings from its Scandinavian operations were up 20 percent compared to last year.
Like-for-like bookings in Canada were 8.0 percent ahead for winter, one of its busiest holiday seasons.
Airtours said it expected passenger volumes for the year to be roughly in line with last year because capacity levels were little changed.

"In reality, we will not end up at the end of the year with the sort of increases that are talked about because we haven't got that sort of increase in capacity available for sale," chairman David Crossland told Reuters in an interview.
"Hopefully, because we've booked more people earlier from brochures, we'll have a better mix of business and a better margin on that business," he added.
Advance brochure bookings are generally more expensive than later sales, which may be offered at steep discounts.
Airtours said it had about 2.8 million passengers out of Britain last year, 1.4 million from Scandinavia and roughly 300,000 out of Canada.
For the first quarter ended December 31, the company managed to cut its pretax loss by about 34 percent to 12.1 million stg.
Airtours attributed the improvement mainly to reduced trading losses at its UK operations, which were hit by high overcapacity levels in the year-earlier period.
"It's been an extremely satisfactory first quarter," deputy chief executive Harry Coe said.
"I think to have reduced our losses is a not inconsiderable achievement. Demand in the marketplace is quite strong at the moment, and forward bookings also reflect that," he added.
Airtours normally reports losses in the first half of its financial year and profits in the second half due to tourists' preference to take holidays during the summer months.
The company said it was still on the lookout for possible acquisitions, but declined to comment on whether it had held any talks with other firms.
"We have a strong balance sheet, very strong cash reserves, and we're interested in growing our business in other European countries and also in the large North American market," Crossland said.

The company added that it was still in talks on its previously-announced plan to buy Italian cruise line Costa Crociere SpA as part of an Anglo-American partnership with Carnival Corp's Carnival Cruises.
